subject: Differentiating MVPA from off-road motorcycle transport

messages.author: cf94dbf4e11f1380
messages.subject: Differentiating MVPA from off-road motorcycle transport
parts:
Hi all,

I would be grateful if anyone has any suggestions that might help me. I have searched this group but I don't believe this question has been asked before.

I am about to start a study looking at 24-hour movement behaviour in Malawi. We will be measuring participant's activity over 7 days, using Axivity AX3 wrist-worn accelerometers on their dominant wrist. We plan to analyse the output using GGIR. We will be recording at 100Hz, with a range +/-8g. Currently using GGIR version 3.1.0 (I realise I need to update this).

However, our study is split across a rural and an urban site. In the rural site, particularly, the main form of motorised transport is by motorbike, on dirt tracks. I have been out with the field team on the back of one of their bikes while wearing an accelerometer, and when I processed the data with GGIR, I noticed on the 'file summary report' (which I've attached) that the period of time corresponding to me being on the motorbike (around 09:00 - 10:00am and 15:00 - 16:00 on Tuesday 25th June) seem to have been identified as moderate PA. 

I wondered about reducing the sampling range, but on the same day I went for a run and the acceleration is similar or possibly even higher (between around 17:00 - 18:00 on the visual report).

Does anyone have any experience or suggestions of how to exclude or differentiate physical activity from motorcycle transport? My understanding is that travel by car is usually filtered out (presumably because of the smoother nature of the acceleration? - although I am not entirely sure how this is done.)

Many thanks!
Ben
